institutionName: Institut d'études politiques de Paris (Sciences Po)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to learn French and live in Paris

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I had a few course registration problems, but besides that everything went fine

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received help switching courses from the Erasmus coordinator

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was difficult and expensive to find housing in Paris as I had to pay agency fees to get access to most accommodation options. I was lucky to find my accommodation in a Facebook group and not get scammed.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: You can't live on campus in Paris, so it's the only option. But it was nice having an appartment.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was extremely stressfull, especially when I didn't know anything about what to do so I didn't end up getting any of my preferred courses. But I think they have changed to system now, so hopefully it will be better in the future.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Everyone got access at the same time, and then you just had to be really quick to sign up to what you wanted. I didn't know which courses were popular so clearly had a bad strategy, and most of my exchange friends also ended up with really random courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I think I only got one of the classes I initially wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I think they are changing the system, otherwise just really prioritze signing up to the one you want the most right away as quickly as you can. And have a long list of other options.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Most of my classes had almost no curriculum. Instead, we had to do tons of group projects, presentations, and random assignments that we usually weren't warned about beforehand. Most of the classes didn't feel very academic, and the level was not very high. I missed diving into academic discussions and studying theories etc.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Teaching was very discussion and presentation based, so there was a high expectation of participation which was nice, but I also like the UCPH approach of teaching and expecting students to read the curriculum

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: It was just really expensive to live in Paris overall

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Cafes and restaurants were generally cheaper than in CPH, but I went out and ate out a lot so expect to spend a lot of money

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I think almost everything, but I didn't really participate in anything. It was also really difficult to sign up for eg. sports activities

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I didn't particpate in any

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on trips to other parts of France (you can sign up for monthly unlimited TGV train tickets for young people so I would definitely recommend doing that). Go to all the museums and cultural activities

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was no problem

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I mostly socialized with local students in my classes, otherwise I made most of my friends during welcome week. It was really expensive to participate in, but it was key to getting a social life

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I think it was overall not complicated

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The boulangeries

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: It is expensive to live in Paris, but it is also way more fun if you just let yourself spend money. Expect a ton of group work and generally SciencesPo requires so many hand-ins, group projects, and mandatory homework as well as mandatory participation in all sessions that school ended up taking most of my time so be prepared for that. French people in Paris didn't want to speak French which was disappointing

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not apart from what I have mentioned already

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Probably all the cool and interesting people I met from all over the world

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The high volume of especially group work in all of my courses in really big groups. No one had time to meet, everyone was stressed about it, I had to many meetings late at night and early in the morning, made sooo many powerpoints, and could never expect people to actually come prepared so so much time was wasted.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
